title: Kth Smallest Across Sorted Lists
statement:
You are given several lists of numbers, `lists`, and **each list is already sorted** from smallest to largest (a list may be empty). Imagine pouring all the numbers into one big sorted sequence (repeats count).

Return the **`k`-th smallest number** of that combined sequence, counting from 1.
constraints: -1000000000 <= values <= 1000000000, each inner list sorted in non-decreasing order

hints.nudge: The smallest number overall is one of the first elements of the lists. After taking it, what is the next candidate?
hints.pattern: A min-heap holding the current front element of each list; pop k times.
hints.pseudocode:
heap = [(list[0], list index, 0) for each non-empty list]
repeat k times: (value, i, j) = pop smallest; if j + 1 < len(list i): push (list i [j+1], i, j+1)
return the last popped value
hints.walkthrough: Merging everything into one array and sorting costs O(N log N). Because every list is sorted, the next smallest number overall is always the front of some list. Keep a min-heap with one entry per list (its current front). Pop the smallest, then push the next element of that same list. After k pops, the last popped value is the k-th smallest. With m lists the heap holds at most m items, so each step costs O(log m) and the total is O(k log m).
